entries.safeUserCheck: Stop using the affected appliance function and contact the Service Centre. Do not open or repair the hob.

evidenceToRequest: photo of error code E4 on the display
product model and serial number
description of when the error appeared
description of checks already completed

entries.problem: Error code E2 is displayed
entries.possibleCause: The supply voltage is incorrect.
entries.safeUserCheck: Do not test live electrical voltage yourself. Have the electrical supply checked safely by an appropriately qualified person.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim or arrange qualified electrical inspection if error E2 remains or the correct supply cannot be confirmed safely.
evidenceToRequest: photo of error code E2 on the display
product model and serial number
description of when the error appeared
description of any recent electrical supply issue

evidenceToRequest: photo of error code E3 on the display

entries.problem: Error code E6 is displayed
entries.possibleCause: The hob has overheated.
entries.safeUserCheck: Stop cooking and allow the hob to cool down completely before using it again.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim if error E6 returns after the hob has completely cooled.
evidenceToRequest: photo of error code E6 on the display
product model and serial number
selected cooking settings
description of whether the code returned after cooling

entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim if error E9 returns after the hob has completely cooled.
evidenceToRequest: photo of error code E9 on the display
product model and serial number
selected cooking settings
description of whether the code returned after cooling

entries.problem: The induction hob does not work
entries.possibleCause: There may be no power supply to the appliance.
entries.safeUserCheck: Check the household fuse or circuit breaker. Do not open the hob or work on its electrical connections.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim if the hob still does not work after the household power protection has been checked.
evidenceToRequest: photo or video showing that the hob does not operate
product model and serial number
description of the household fuse or circuit-breaker check

entries.problem: The touch sensor fields do not respond
entries.possibleCause: The appliance may not be switched on, a sensor may have been touched for less than one second, or several sensors may have been touched at the same time.
entries.safeUserCheck: Switch the appliance on. Touch one sensor at a time and hold it slightly longer, except where the manual specifically requires simultaneous sensors.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim if the sensors remain unresponsive after the documented operating checks.
evidenceToRequest: video showing the unresponsive controls
product model and serial number
description of the control checks already completed

entries.problem: The hob does not respond and emits a long acoustic signal
entries.possibleCause: The controls may have been operated incorrectly, or one or more sensor fields may be covered or dirty.
entries.safeUserCheck: Make sure the sensor fields are uncovered and clean, then switch the hob on again and operate the sensors as described in the manual.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim if the long signal and lack of response continue after the controls are clean and correctly operated.
evidenceToRequest: video or audio of the long acoustic signal
photo of the control panel
product model and serial number
description of cleaning and restart checks

entries.problem: The whole hob switches itself off
entries.possibleCause: No setting may have been entered shortly after switching the appliance on, or the sensor fields may be covered or dirty.
entries.safeUserCheck: Make sure the sensor fields are uncovered and clean. Switch the control panel on again and enter the required setting without delay.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim if the hob continues switching itself off after the controls have been cleaned and used as described.
evidenceToRequest: video showing the hob switching off
photo of the control panel
product model and serial number
description of checks already completed

entries.problem: A cooking zone switches off automatically and H is displayed
entries.possibleCause: The operating-time limit may have been reached, sensor fields may be covered or dirty, or electronic components may have overheated.
entries.safeUserCheck: Keep the sensor fields clean and uncovered. If the zone has switched off because of the operating-time limit, switch it on again when safe. If overheating is suspected, allow the hob to cool before using it again.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim if the cooking zone repeatedly switches off after the hob has cooled and the controls are clean and unobstructed.
evidenceToRequest: photo or video showing H and the affected cooking zone
product model and serial number
selected heat setting
description of whether the hob was allowed to cool
description of control-panel checks

entries.problem: The display shows H after cooking
entries.possibleCause: H is the residual heat indicator and means the glass around the cooking zone is still hot.
entries.safeUserCheck: Do not touch the cooking zone and do not place heat-sensitive objects on it while H is displayed. Allow the cooking zone to cool.
entries.claimTrigger: No service claim is required for the normal residual heat indicator.

entries.problem: The residual heat indicator is not displayed even though a cooking zone may still be hot
entries.possibleCause: A power outage occurred or the appliance was disconnected from the power supply.
entries.safeUserCheck: Treat the cooking zones as potentially hot even when H is not displayed after a power outage. Do not touch them until they have cooled.
entries.claimTrigger: No claim is required when the missing H indicator is caused by a power outage or disconnection as described by the manual.
entries.sourceSection: PDF pp. 42 and 46, RESIDUAL HEAT INDICATOR

entries.problem: The glass-ceramic hob surface is cracked, chipped, or broken
entries.possibleCause: The cooking surface has been physically damaged. The manual warns that liquids can reach live electrical parts through damaged areas and create an electric-shock hazard.
entries.safeUserCheck: Stop using the hob immediately and disconnect it from the power supply using the plug or main circuit breaker if this can be done safely. Do not touch, repair, or continue using the cracked surface.
entries.claimTrigger: Create an urgent service claim for any crack, break, or chip in the cooking surface.
evidenceToRequest: photo of the cracked or chipped glass
product model and serial number
description of how the damage occurred
description of whether the hob was in use when the damage occurred
entries.sourceSection: PDF pp. 32-34 and 46, SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS / TROUBLESHOOTING

entries.problem: The cooking zone does not detect the cookware
entries.possibleCause: There may be no cookware on the active zone, the cookware may not be suitable for induction, or its ferromagnetic base may be too small for the cooking zone.
entries.safeUserCheck: Use induction-compatible cookware with a flat ferromagnetic base. If the cookware is not detected on one zone, try a cooking zone with a suitably smaller diameter as described in the manual.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim if known suitable cookware is still not detected on appropriate cooking zones.
evidenceToRequest: photo or video of the cookware-detection indication
photo of the cookware base or induction marking
product model and serial number
description of cookware tested and cooking zones used
entries.sourceSection: PDF pp. 40-42, BASIC INFORMATION ABOUT YOUR APPLIANCE - Cookware characteristics / If the appliance does not detect the cookware on the operating cooking zone

entries.problem: A cooking zone switches off about one minute after no suitable cookware is detected
entries.possibleCause: The hob is designed to switch the active cooking zone off after approximately one minute if suitable cookware is not placed on it.
entries.safeUserCheck: Place suitable induction cookware on the cooking zone. No corrective action is needed if the automatic switch-off occurs because no suitable cookware is present.
entries.claimTrigger: No service claim is required for this normal automatic behaviour.
matchTerms: zone turns off after one minute
entries.sourceSection: PDF p. 42, IF THE APPLIANCE DOES NOT DETECT THE COOKWARE ON THE OPERATING COOKING ZONE

entries.problem: The controls are locked and most touch sensors do not operate
entries.possibleCause: The Child Lock function is active.
entries.safeUserCheck: Touch and hold the Child Lock sensor for 3 seconds to deactivate the lock. The On/Off control remains available for emergency switch-off.
entries.claimTrigger: No service claim is required if the controls work normally after the Child Lock is deactivated.

entries.problem: The Child Lock needs to be deactivated
entries.possibleCause: The Child Lock has been enabled.
entries.safeUserCheck: Touch and hold the Child Lock sensor for 3 seconds until the lock indication disappears.
entries.claimTrigger: No service claim is required for normal Child Lock deactivation.

entries.problem: A cooking zone switches off automatically after operating for a long time
entries.possibleCause: Each cooking zone has a safety operating-time limit based on the selected heat setting. The function cannot be disabled.
entries.safeUserCheck: If the cooking zone switched off because the documented operating-time limit was reached, switch the zone on again when it is safe to continue cooking.
entries.claimTrigger: No service claim is required for the normal safety auto-off function.
entries.sourceSection: PDF p. 45, OPERATION - Cooking zone auto off

entries.problem: Booster power automatically drops to heat setting 9
entries.possibleCause: The Booster function operates for a maximum of 5 minutes and then automatically reduces the cooking-zone power to level 9.
entries.safeUserCheck: No corrective action is required if Booster reduces to level 9 after its maximum operating period.
entries.claimTrigger: No service claim is required for this normal Booster behaviour.

entries.problem: The induction hob makes a buzzing or rough fan sound
entries.possibleCause: The cooling fan is operating to cool the internal electronic components.
entries.safeUserCheck: No corrective action is required when the sound matches the normal cooling-fan noise described by the manual.
entries.claimTrigger: Do not create a service claim for normal cooling-fan noise alone.

entries.problem: The induction hob makes hissing or whistling sounds during cooking
entries.possibleCause: When several cooking zones are used at full power, the operating frequency of the induction coils can produce hissing or whistling sounds. The exact sound can also depend on the cookware and heat setting.
entries.safeUserCheck: No corrective action is required if the sound matches the normal induction sounds described by the manual.
entries.claimTrigger: Do not create a service claim for normal induction hissing or whistling alone.
entries.sourceSection: PDF pp. 40 and 46, BASIC INFORMATION ABOUT YOUR APPLIANCE - Induction hob operation principle / TROUBLESHOOTING

entries.problem: An odour is released when the hob is used for the first time
entries.possibleCause: The manual states that a temporary odour may be released during the first start-up.
entries.safeUserCheck: Ventilate the room or open a window. The manual states that the odour is temporary.
entries.claimTrigger: No service claim is required for the temporary first-use odour described by the manual. Stop using the appliance if there is smoke, burning, or another abnormal safety hazard.
entries.sourceSection: PDF p. 42, BEFORE USING THE APPLIANCE FOR THE FIRST TIME

entries.problem: The hob controls cannot be operated while the appliance is switched on
entries.possibleCause: The manual does not specify a customer-repairable technical cause for complete control failure.
entries.safeUserCheck: Stop using the appliance. Switch off the main circuit breaker or remove the fuse if this can be done safely and contact customer service. Do not open or repair the hob.
entries.claimTrigger: Create an urgent service claim if the hob cannot be safely controlled or switched as intended.
evidenceToRequest: video showing the control failure if safe to record
product model and serial number
description of the control failure
description of checks already completed
entries.sourceSection: PDF p. 49, CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE - Periodic inspections

entries.problem: The hob does not work and the cooking zones cannot be switched on or operated
entries.possibleCause: The troubleshooting table identifies faulty electronics as the cause.
entries.safeUserCheck: Reset the appliance by disconnecting it from the mains for a few minutes using the household fuse or circuit breaker. Do not open the appliance.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim if the cooking zones still cannot be operated after the supported reset.
evidenceToRequest: video showing that the cooking zones cannot be operated
product model and serial number
description of the reset already completed
description of any display indications

entries.problem: There is fire, smoke, or burning on or around the hob
entries.possibleCause: The manual warns that unattended cooking with fat or oil can result in fire.
entries.safeUserCheck: Stop using the appliance. Never attempt to extinguish a cooking fire with water. Switch off the appliance if this can be done safely and cover the flame with a lid or fire blanket as described by the manual.
entries.claimTrigger: Create an urgent claim and stop using the appliance when there is fire, smoke, burning, or related heat damage.
evidenceToRequest: photo of visible damage only after the situation is safe
product model and serial number
description of what happened
description of any visible heat or fire damage

entries.problem: A hob fault remains after the supported troubleshooting checks
entries.possibleCause: The manual does not specify a customer-repairable cause for faults that remain after the documented checks.
entries.safeUserCheck: Disconnect the appliance from the power supply and contact the nearest service centre. Do not dismantle or repair electrical components yourself.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim when a fault remains after the safe checks described in the manual.
evidenceToRequest: photo or video showing the fault
product model and serial number
description of the problem
description of checks already completed
entries.sourceSection: PDF pp. 46 and 50, TROUBLESHOOTING / WARRANTY AND AFTER SALES SERVICE
